### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. Waardenburg syndrome type 2E  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.792)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:11190)

**Proposed mechanism:** SOX10 (HGNC:11190) —DISRUPTS→ SOX10 transcriptional regulation of neural crest development (GO:0007411); SOX10 transcriptional regulation of neural crest development (GO:0007411) —LEADS_TO→ Pigmentation defect (HP:0001007); SOX10 transcriptional regulation of neural crest development (GO:0007411) —LEADS_TO→ Hirschsprung disease (HP:0002260); SOX10 transcriptional regulation of neural crest development (GO:0007411) —LEADS_TO→ Craniofacial abnormalities (HP:0000252). Loss-of-function mutations in SOX10 disrupt its normal transcriptional activity, impacting the development of neural crest cells. This disruption leads to a spectrum of phenotypes including pigmentation defects (Waardenburg syndrome type 2E) and neurocristopathies like Hirschsprung disease and craniofacial abnormalities (Segmentation and neurodevelopmental disorder 1).

**How to falsify it:** The identification of a specific pathogenic variant in SOX10 that is present in gnomAD with a frequency greater than 1% would falsify the hypothesis that this variant causes these rare diseases. _(variant: rs123456789)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of SOX10 in these distinct but related neurocristopathies could inform therapeutic strategies targeting common developmental pathways for both conditions.

#### 2. PCWH syndrome  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.786)

**Proposed mechanism:** SOX10 (HGNC:11190) —DISRUPTS→ Transcriptional regulation of neural development (GO:0007411); Transcriptional regulation of neural development (GO:0007411) —LEADS_TO→ Intellectual disability (HP:0001249); Transcriptional regulation of neural development (GO:0007411) —LEADS_TO→ Hypoplastic or absent corpus callosum (HP:0002079). Haploinsufficiency of SOX10 (HGNC:11190) disrupts the critical pathway of transcriptional regulation of neural development (GO:0007411), leading to the shared phenotypes of intellectual disability (HP:0001249) and hypoplastic or absent corpus callosum (HP:0002079) observed in both MONDO:0013202 and PCWH syndrome (MONDO:0012198).

**How to falsify it:** If pathogenic variants in SOX10 are not found to be causative for both MONDO:0013202 and PCWH syndrome (MONDO:0012198) with consistent haploinsufficiency effects, this hypothesis would be falsified. _(variant: Exome or genome sequencing studies showing a high allele frequency (>1%) of pathogenic variants in HGNC:11190 in general populations would also challenge this hypothesis.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of SOX10 in both diseases can inform therapeutic strategies targeting neural development, potentially leading to treatments for both conditions.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that mutations in SMARCA4 and SOX10 affect entirely distinct and non-overlapping cellular or molecular pathways critical for neuronal development, or the absence of intellectual disability in individuals with pathogenic variants in these genes. _(variant: N/A)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of SMARCA4 and SOX10 in neuronal development could lead to the identification of common therapeutic targets or strategies for intellectual disability associated with defects in these genes.

**How to falsify it:** Discovery of pathogenic variants in SOX10 that are exclusively associated with one disease and not the other, or if genetic studies reveal completely independent molecular pathways for each disease that do not converge at the level of Schwann cell differentiation or myelination. _(variant: Pathogenic variants in SOX10 with a minor allele frequency > 0.01% in gnomAD.)_
